quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
Use only the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Look multiple times if needed. Watch both the traffic in front of you and the traffic in the lane next to you.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Side mirrors eliminate blind spots completely.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign appears on vehicles that move slowly.

questions.question: What does this sign indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers about hazards or special conditions ahead. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid staying beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside them for extended periods.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can cross completely before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?
questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces abilities needed for safe driving. Alcohol travels from your stomach to your blood, then to other body parts. It affects the brain areas that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and harms concentration and alertness.

questions.question: After holding your license for six months, which passenger cannot be in your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Your 18-year-old friend.
questions.explanation: During the first six months, a new driver may only have a driving instructor, parents or guardians, or someone at least 20 years old with certain restrictions. During months seven through twelve, only immediate family members can be additional passengers.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent will:

options.text: Have no effect on your driving.
Not put other drivers at risk.
Double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either lane.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only drivers next to the broken line may pass.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no more than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing before you go. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: If you need your lights on while driving due to weather or darkness, use:
questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, causing glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, give the right-of-way to:
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: Drivers should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at a curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to match the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: If you drive slower than the traffic around you, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when needed for safety, but if you block normal traffic movement, you can get a ticket. Match traffic speed unless traffic exceeds the speed limit.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may go if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow allows you to go in that direction if you are in the correct lane. Always yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means passing is not allowed. Sometimes both lines are solid, meaning no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see traffic around you. Release the accelerator and move to the brake pedal. Brake with steady pressure for a smooth stop.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Park completely off the road, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park completely off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: Move your car completely off the road if you can. Keep all four wheels away from the driving surface.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, what is the only way to reduce alcohol's effects?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not speed this up. One drink takes about one hour to leave your system.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge and slow down.
Drive to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then stop.

questions.question: You stopped for a train at a railroad crossing. After the train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Another train may be coming on a different track. Wait until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing before you go.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your car. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to see blind spots before changing lanes.
